quote:
[Harsha Gaddipati](https://www.linkedin.com/in/harsha-gaddipati-032bb820a/?lipi=urn%3Ali%3Apage%3Ad_flagship3_search_srp_people%3BjEmLKN1wSFaYb%2B6BLHyeFw%3D%3D), cofounder and CEO of [Slashy](https://www.slashy.com/), sprained both of his wrists in February. He was playing basketball in loafers, which isn't the wisest decision he's ever made. He couldn't type for over a month. Fortunately, the email client he had built by hand could cover for him. "I was in immense pain, but I didn't miss a day of work," [he said](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/harsha-gaddipati-032bb820a_sprained-both-my-wrists-luckily-slashy-share-7424339442074697728-ZgFL/).

Slashy (not to be confused with Slash) is an AI-native email client based in San Francisco and backed by Y Combinator, where it went through the Summer 2025 batch. Ever since AI started scaling as quickly as it did in the early 2020's, email has been one of the most obvious places to put it. That's why so many have taken a run at it -- Gmail got Gemini a while back, Outlook got CoPilot, and Grammarly bought Superhuman.

However, Slashy goes far beyond the quick summaries, grammar fixes, and one-sentence reply suggestions of the more popular
